chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When the sun is fully eclipsed and burned out, and you did not know [about it], and you knew afterwards, then you must make up [the prayer]; and if it did not fully burn out, then there is no making up upon you."

This is the report, and that which we mentioned earlier from the narration of Hariz came as two detailed reports, and the hadith of 'there is no making up upon him' is general, and the ruling of the detailed [report] over the general is more preferable.

key_terms.اِحْتَرَقَتْ: burned out / consumed (referring to the sun's disk)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for making up the solar eclipse prayer if one missed it due to ignorance?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific condition for Qada (making up) the solar eclipse prayer: it is obligatory only if the eclipse was total and the observer was unaware, whereas partial eclipses do not require makeup. Shaykh al-Tusi highlights the jurisprudential principle of preferring the detailed report (al-mufassal) over the general one (al-mujmal) to resolve apparent discrepancies in the chain of transmission. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on precise conditions in ritual obligations, linking the physical phenomenon of the eclipse to the legal necessity of awareness.
